clue.text: Salt I whisked with ice to make compound

indicators.note: whisked means stirred up, so the letters of the words before and after are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook beats salt into ice to produce some compound, like a kitchen chemistry experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A silicate is a chemical compound of silicon, oxygen and a metal, the stuff of most rocks.

clue.text: Love goddess in Scottish tartan

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of letters of Scottish tartan

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A goddess of love dressed in a kilt or plaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Ishtar was the Babylonian deity of love, fertility and war.

clue.text: Largely wet and fertile, suitable for sporting?

indicators.note: largely means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
arable land is fertile enough to be ploughed and cropped

explanation.surface: Describing soggy, rich farmland and asking whether it would do for sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporting' here means wearing, as in sporting a hat, so suitable for sporting is something you can wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing that can be worn, that is sported, is wearable; the question mark flags this playful sense.

clue.text: Bring up obsessive to understand

indicators.note: in a down clue bringing up a word turns it to read from bottom to top

parts.note: a wonk is someone obsessively studious about a subject, a policy wonk

explanation.surface: Raising an obsessive child so they come to understand things.
explanation.definitionFit: To know something is to understand or grasp it.

clue.text: Talk about the French ski lodge?

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the talk word goes round the French article

parts.note: a chat is a talk
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Chatting about a ski lodge in the Alps, with a French flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is the wooden Alpine house typically used for a skiing holiday; the question mark notes it is one example of a chalet.

clue.text: Singer or instrumentalist initially loves getting to grips with this music

indicators.note: getting to grips with means holding tight, so the two loves enclose the rest

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so two loves give two O's
a rat is an informer, someone who sings to the police
taken as written

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of instrumentalist

explanation.surface: A singer or player who loves tackling this kind of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' looks musical but it is underworld slang: an informer sings, and a rat is an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large choral work, often sacred, for singers and orchestra, such as Handel's Messiah.

clue.text: North Dakota's right about tree

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the right goes round the state abbreviation

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
ND is the postal abbreviation for North Dakota

explanation.surface: A legal claim that North Dakota has a right concerning a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Linden is another name for the lime tree, common in parks and avenues.

clue.text: A German mug? Definitely not!

parts.note: ein is German for a
a stein is a large beer mug

explanation.surface: Asking whether some German is a fool, and firmly answering no.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, the German for a plus a beer mug; read as a whole, a German who was certainly no mug, that is no fool.
explanation.definitionFit: The German-born physicist is the byword for genius, the very opposite of a mug or simpleton.

clue.text: Daring fellow Republic caught

parts.note: he refers to a male, a fellow
ROI is the usual abbreviation for the Republic of Ireland
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A daring man from the Republic gets caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroic acts are bold and courageous, showing great bravery.

clue.text: Land with recurrent wet season

parts.note: to land a prize is to win it

indicators.note: recurrent means running back, so the word for wet reads backwards

parts.note: to ret is to soak flax or hemp in water

explanation.surface: A country with a rainy season that keeps coming round.
explanation.definitionFit: Winter is the coldest of the four seasons of the year.

clue.text: Prosperous container business

parts.note: a well holds water, so it is a container of sorts
a to-do is a fuss or carry-on, a business

explanation.surface: A firm that makes containers is doing well.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-to-do describes people who are wealthy and comfortably off.

clue.text: Starts to have an interest researching old musical

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: Beginning to take an interest in researching a vintage stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair is the 1967 rock musical of the hippie era, famous for 'Aquarius'.

clue.text: Minor celebrity in Gulf, very hot

parts.note: a B-lister is a second-tier celebrity
G is Golf in the radio alphabet, here a near-sounding gulf; G is also a common abbreviation for gulf on maps

explanation.surface: A minor celebrity sweltering somewhere in the Gulf states.
explanation.definitionFit: Blistering heat is intense enough to raise blisters, so extremely hot.

clue.text: Part of Antrim, a rich source of ceramic

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wealthy area of County Antrim, in Northern Ireland, known for pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Imari is the Japanese port that gave its name to a richly decorated porcelain.

clue.text: Use announced for trees

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: the word use, said out loud

explanation.surface: A declaration of what the trees are to be used for.
explanation.definitionFit: Yews are evergreen conifers often found in churchyards.

clue.text: Feeling excited — new couple moving in

indicators.note: moving in says the couple and the new letter take up residence inside the excited word

parts.note: sent is slang for thrilled or excited
to tie is to couple or join

explanation.surface: Thrilled because a newly married pair is moving into the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentient being is able to perceive and feel things.

clue.text: Cut back document for orals?

indicators.note: back means turned round, so the cutting word reads backwards

parts.note: to axe is to cut
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a document

explanation.surface: Trimming a document down for oral presentations.
explanation.definitionFit: Orals are spoken tests, one kind of examination; the question mark marks them as an example.

clue.text: Surrender the right to indicate short method

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to signal is to indicate
a way of doing something is a method

explanation.surface: Giving up a legal right in order to show a quicker procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign away a claim or property is to give it up formally by signing a document.

clue.text: As of blundering clumsy people

indicators.note: blundering means stumbling about, so the letters stumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A grammatical aside about awkward, bumbling people.
explanation.definitionFit: Oafs are stupid, ungainly louts.

clue.text: Silly fellow officer commanding sea crossing

indicators.note: crossing means spanning, so the sea stretches either side of the officer

parts.note: the Aral Sea in central Asia
CIC is commander-in-chief, the top commanding officer

explanation.surface: A daft officer in charge of a ferry across the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Farcical means absurd or ridiculous, like a farce on stage.

clue.text: Extravagantly praising man, lacking a motive

indicators.note: extravagantly means wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order
lacking says the letter of the next word is left out of the jumbled pool

explanation.surface: Lavish praise heaped on a man who has no motive.
explanation.definitionFit: The mainspring of something is its chief driving force or motivation.

clue.text: Facial expression as muscle tightens to begin with

parts.note: a pec is a pectoral, a chest muscle

indicators.note: to begin with means take only the first letter of tightens

explanation.surface: A face changes as its muscles tighten.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspect means the look or appearance of a face, its expression.

clue.text: In spring, laid up fertiliser

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the result reads from bottom to top
In says the second word goes inside the spring word

parts.note: a hop is a spring or jump
sat, as in set or placed down, stands for laid

explanation.surface: Something was stored away in spring for later use as fertiliser.
explanation.definitionFit: Potash is a potassium compound widely spread on fields as a plant nutrient.

clue.text: The side needs changing in a month — this group decides

indicators.note: needs changing says one side swaps for the other, left giving way to right

parts.note: July is a month
L for left is one side; it changes to R for right

explanation.surface: A team that must reorganise within a month.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury is the panel that decides the verdict in a trial.

clue.text: Two girls sharing an instrument

parts.note: Jo is one girl's name, the first of two
Anna is the second girl's name

explanation.surface: Two girls taking turns on one instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Two names are needed: JO and ANNA. Joanna is rhyming slang for piano, from London Cockney.
explanation.definitionFit: Joanna is Cockney rhyming slang for a piano, a keyboard instrument.

clue.text: After university paid, inside I felt strangely happy

indicators.note: after means the rest of the letters follow the university letter
inside means the jumbled letters are put within the paid abbreviation

parts.note: PD is the abbreviation for paid

indicators.note: strangely means oddly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Once a student loan was repaid, a graduate felt oddly elated.
explanation.definitionFit: Uplifted means cheered or raised in spirits, so elated.

clue.text: No this is ineffective: cut into small pieces

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the idiom for something that fails or is no use
second meaning: to ... food is to chop it into cubes

explanation.surface: Declaring a chopping method useless.
explanation.definitionFit: The word completes the phrase 'no dice', meaning no luck, and is also the cook's verb for cubing.

clue.text: A group of spies hide a camera at first in a shrub

indicators.note: hide means conceal inside, so the spies enclose the rest

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency

indicators.note: at first means just the initial letter of camera

explanation.surface: Spies conceal a camera inside a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Acacia is a thorny shrub or tree, the wattle of Australia.

clue.text: Prospects of play?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: views or vistas, as a landscape scene
second meaning: the divisions of a play's acts

explanation.surface: Wondering about the chances of a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenes are both views of landscape and the subdivisions of a stage drama.

clue.text: Spooner's sensible boring task for tool

indicators.note: Spooner's says swap the opening sounds of the two words, after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: sane means sensible; said aloud it can be written as a different spelling
a chore is a dull job; in a non-rhotic British accent it is said the same as a different spelling

explanation.surface: A tool recommended for a dull but sensible job.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of SANE CHORE gives 'chain sore', which in a British accent is said like the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A chainsaw is a powered cutting implement with teeth on a moving loop.
